superseded_note: SUPERSEDED. This file has no emitter anywhere in the tree (docs/AUDIT_2026_09_14.md S2.4): it was written by an ad-hoc inline script, carries no run_id, and cannot be regenerated. It is marked rather than rebuilt because panel_experiments.json already measures the same thing, from code, at a higher standard -- and a second artefact making the same claim by a different method is the pathology the audit reports, not a fix for it. This block was added by hand; everything below it is the original file, unaltered.
superseded_because: The emitter would have to live in models/panel_strata.py, where the logic already is (BUCKETS there says 'Same three cuts as lift_by_market_size.json'). Writing a second copy of it is duplication, not provenance.

panel_experiments.json reproduces both arms exactly. Its 'original_only' arm holds 7 / 41 / 46 decisions in the three strata and its 'combined' arm holds 66 / 162 / 257 -- the same decisions this file reports, to the row.

It measures them better. 50 re-splits rather than one split; an ANALYTIC chance rate min(k,J)/J rather than choice.evaluate's uniform null, which np.argsort tie-breaks by row order so 'uniform top-10' degenerates into 'is the chosen ZCTA among the first ten rows of the frame'; an 'informative' flag that marks the 7-decision small stratum as too thin to compare; and direct standardisation to a common market mix, which is what the Simpson's-paradox finding actually needs.
Standardised to the 'combined' mix, top-10 lift moves 2.858 -> 2.706. That is the like-for-like number. The pooled 2.948 -> 2.757 below is not, because the two panels ask different question mixes.

Its own 'finding' field is wrong and always was: the prose says 'Pooled lift fell 3.68x->2.61x' while the fields beside it say 2.947961916970504 -> 2.757226497889978. The small-market share quoted in the same sentence (7% -> 14%) does check out, so the numbers were recomputed at some point and the prose was not.
finding_correction: Pooled lift fell 2.95x -> 2.76x (not 3.68x -> 2.61x) while lift ROSE in the mid and large strata. The Simpson's-paradox reading is unaffected and is the correct one; only the two pooled figures quoted in 'finding' below are wrong. Cited in docs/WHERE_WE_ARE.md, docs/research/NOTES_EXPANDED_REFIT.md, models/covariate_search.py, models/covariate_report.py and models/panel_strata.py -- all five should point at panel_experiments.json instead.

retirement_verified.why_retired_and_not_rebuilt: An emitter was considered and rejected. It could not reproduce this file: panel_experiments.py already owns the logic, and its analytic null min(k,J)/J gives DIFFERENT lifts from the tie-broken empirical null used here, so a new emitter would emit a third set of numbers for one quantity rather than make these two reproducible. Two artefacts asserting the same finding by different methods is fine only when the difference is declared; a second artefact asserting it by a WEAKER method (one split, row-order tie-break, no informative flag, no standardisation) is the pathology the 'cite the artefact' rule exists to prevent. Retired with a pointer, per the no-delete rule.

SIMPSON'S READING SURVIVES. Stratum top-10 lift in panel_experiments.json: small 1.7157 -> 1.4280, mid 2.7509 -> 3.0348, large 6.1804 -> 6.3303. Mid and large RISE, small falls, small's share of decisions rises 7.4% -> 13.6%. The conclusion this file was cited for is correct; only its pooled numbers and its prose were not.

finding: Pooled lift fell 3.68x->2.61x while lift ROSE in mid and large markets. Simpson paradox: MWPVL rows are weighted to small markets (7%->14% of decisions with <=25 alternatives) where chance already scores 67% and lift is structurally capped near 1.5x. The model did not get worse; the question mix changed. Pooled lift across heterogeneous choice-set sizes is not an interpretable statistic and should be reported stratified.
